rawRetro.summary: ESLint failed because shared/*.ts sat outside every TypeScript project. Nested shared/tsconfig.json plus tsconfig.server.json include, and four type-aware lint fixes, restored the lint stage.

improvements.title: Project-service lint of new top-level source trees
improvements.detail: Adding a directory such as shared/ that is not in the template layout is invisible to ESLint until a nested tsconfig.json exists. The first failure is a project-service parse error on every file, not a real rule.
improvements.suggestedChange: When introducing a new top-level TypeScript tree, add the nested tsconfig (like server/ and database/) and include it in the emitting tsconfig.server.json in the same change as the first source file.

issues.title: shared/ not found by ESLint project service
issues.symptom: eslint . failed with 20 parse errors: shared/*.ts was not found by the project service; consider including it in tsconfig.json or allowDefaultProject.
issues.rootCause: Domain rules were added under shared/ but no tsconfig included those files. Root tsconfig.json only includes client/; tsconfig.server.json only included server, database, and cli. ESLint projectService therefore had no project for shared/.
issues.resolution: Added shared/tsconfig.json extending tsconfig.server.json, included shared/**/*.ts in tsconfig.server.json, documented the layout in .agents/rules/shared.md, and fixed four type-aware lint errors that appeared once the files were type-checked (no-base-to-string, unused GoalTargets, unnecessary assertion).
